key_insight: Long-range ML interatomic potentials better capture electrostatic defect interactions in SrTiO3 than short-range models, especially when tested beyond idealized systems into realistic DFT-based defect energetics.
engineering_relevance: Accurate defect-transport predictions in perovskite oxides require models that retain Coulombic and screening effects, which is critical for vacancy migration, reliability, and electronic materials design.
method: Benchmarked MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES, and LOREM against a short-range MACE baseline.
Progressed from synthetic point-charge systems to first-principles SrTiO3 defect structures with Sr–O Schottky vacancy pairs.
Evaluated oxygen-vacancy migration barriers using CI-NEB and molecular dynamics as a function of vacancy-pair separation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic comparison on both synthetic electrostatic tests and DFT data for SrTiO3 defects, including migration-barrier calculations that probe extrapolation beyond training-like configurations.
watch_item: Performance on DFT total energies can be confounded by dielectric screening and exchange-correlation contributions, so agreement does not guarantee physically correct long-range charge interactions in all defect environments.
paper_title: Long-Range Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Defect Energetics in SrTiO$_3$
